title: Problem-Solving, Ratios, Rates & Data
sub: 20 FRQs + 25 MCQs • Difficulty Progression • Cross-Lesson Synthesis

sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: In a concrete mix, the ratio of cement to sand to gravel by weight is $1 : 2.5 : 4$. How many kilograms of each material are needed to produce $600\,\mathrm{kg}$ of concrete?
questions.answer: Total ratio parts $= 1 + 2.5 + 4 = 7.5$. Each part equals $\dfrac{600}{7.5} = 80\,\mathrm{kg}$. Thus cement $= 80\,\mathrm{kg}$, sand $= 2.5(80) = 200\,\mathrm{kg}$, and gravel $= 4(80) = 320\,\mathrm{kg}$.

questions.q: Convert a speed of $90\,\mathrm{km/h}$ into meters per second ($\mathrm{m/s}$) and feet per second ($\mathrm{ft/s}$, using $1\,\mathrm{m} \approx 3.28\,\mathrm{ft}$).
questions.answer: $90\,\mathrm{km/h} \times \dfrac{1000\,\mathrm{m}}{1\,\mathrm{km}} \times \dfrac{1\,\mathrm{h}}{3600\,\mathrm{s}} = \dfrac{90{,}000}{3600} = 25\,\mathrm{m/s}$. In feet per second, $25 \times 3.28 = 82.0\,\mathrm{ft/s}$.

questions.q: An electronics store marks up the wholesale cost of a laptop by $40\%$ to set the retail list price, and then offers a $25\%$ holiday discount off the list price. Find the net percentage profit over wholesale cost.
questions.answer: Multiply the sequential scale factors: $1.40 \times (1 - 0.25) = 1.40 \times 0.75 = 1.05$. A combined multiplier of $1.05$ represents a net profit of $5\%$ above wholesale cost.

questions.q: After a $16\%$ price reduction, a laboratory microscope sells for $630$ dollars. What was the original price of the microscope before the reduction?
questions.answer: Let $P_0$ be the original price: $(1 - 0.16)P_0 = 0.84P_0 = 630 \Rightarrow P_0 = \dfrac{630}{0.84} = 750$ dollars.

questions.target: Scale Drawings: Linear vs. Area Scaling
questions.q: On an architectural blueprint drawn at a scale of $1\,\mathrm{cm} : 2.5\,\mathrm{m}$, a rectangular conference room measures $4.8\,\mathrm{cm}$ by $3.2\,\mathrm{cm}$. Find the actual perimeter (in meters) and actual floor area (in $\mathrm{m^2}$) of the room.
questions.answer: Actual length $= 4.8 \times 2.5 = 12\,\mathrm{m}$; actual width $= 3.2 \times 2.5 = 8\,\mathrm{m}$. Actual perimeter $= 2(12 + 8) = 40\,\mathrm{m}$, and actual floor area $= 12 \times 8 = 96\,\mathrm{m^2}$.

questions.q: Pump A can fill a reservoir in $6$ hours, and Pump B can fill the same reservoir in $10$ hours. If both pumps operate together, how many hours does it take to fill the reservoir?
questions.answer: Combined rate: $R = \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{5 + 3}{30} = \dfrac{8}{30} = \dfrac{4}{15}$ reservoir per hour. Time required $= \dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{15}{4} = 3.75$ hours ($3$ hours $45$ minutes).

questions.target: Reading Rates & Percentages from Bar Charts
questions.q: The bar chart below shows quarterly solar energy output (in MWh) for a microgrid across four quarters. Calculate the percentage increase from Q1 to Q3 and the percentage of annual output generated in Q3.
questions.answer: From Q1 ($120\,\mathrm{MWh}$) to Q3 ($192\,\mathrm{MWh}$), the percentage increase is $\dfrac{192 - 120}{120} \times 100\% = 60\%$. Total annual output is $120 + 150 + 192 + 138 = 600\,\mathrm{MWh}$, so Q3 accounts for $\dfrac{192}{600} \times 100\% = 32\%$.

sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Intermediate Modeling (8–14)

questions.q: A metallurgist has $80\,\mathrm{g}$ of a $35\%$ silver alloy. How many grams of pure ($100\%$) silver must be melted into the alloy to raise the silver concentration to $60\%$?
questions.answer: Let $x$ be the grams of pure silver added: $\dfrac{0.35(80) + 1.00x}{80 + x} = 0.60 \Rightarrow 28 + x = 48 + 0.60x \Rightarrow 0.40x = 20 \Rightarrow x = 50\,\mathrm{g}$.

questions.q: The illumination intensity $I$ from a point light source varies inversely as the square of the distance $d$ from the source ($I = k/d^2$). If $I = 180\,\mathrm{lux}$ at $d = 2\,\mathrm{m}$, find $I$ at $d = 6\,\mathrm{m}$, and determine by what percentage $I$ changes when $d$ increases by $25\%$.
questions.answer: At $d = 6\,\mathrm{m}$ ($3$ times the distance), $I = \dfrac{180}{3^2} = 20\,\mathrm{lux}$. When $d$ is multiplied by $1.25 = \dfrac{5}{4}$, $I$ is multiplied by $\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)^2 = \dfrac{16}{25} = 0.64$, which is a $36\%$ decrease.

questions.q: A commuter drives the first $60\,\mathrm{km}$ of a trip at $80\,\mathrm{km/h}$ and the remaining $90\,\mathrm{km}$ at $60\,\mathrm{km/h}$. Compute the total travel time and the overall average speed for the $150\,\mathrm{km}$ trip.
questions.answer: Time for segment 1: $t_1 = \dfrac{60}{80} = 0.75\,\mathrm{h}$. Time for segment 2: $t_2 = \dfrac{90}{60} = 1.50\,\mathrm{h}$. Total time $= 2.25\,\mathrm{h} = \dfrac{9}{4}\,\mathrm{h}$, so overall average speed $= \dfrac{150}{9/4} = \dfrac{600}{9} = \dfrac{200}{3} \approx 66.67\,\mathrm{km/h}$.

questions.q: In a student body of $1{,}200$ students, $65\%$ take Spanish, $45\%$ take French, and $20\%$ take neither language. How many students take both Spanish and French, and what percentage of Spanish students also take French?
questions.answer: Students taking at least one language: $80\%$ of $1{,}200 = 960$. By Inclusion-Exclusion, $65\% + 45\% - b = 80\% \Rightarrow b = 30\%$, which is $0.30(1200) = 360$ students. Among Spanish students ($65\%$), the fraction also taking French is $\dfrac{30\%}{65\%} = \dfrac{6}{13} \approx 46.15\%$.

questions.q: Convert an irrigation flow rate of $450$ gallons per hour into liters per minute, given $1\,\mathrm{gallon} = 3.785\,\mathrm{L}$. Round to two decimal places.
questions.answer: $450\,\dfrac{\mathrm{gal}}{\mathrm{h}} \times \dfrac{3.785\,\mathrm{L}}{1\,\mathrm{gal}} \times \dfrac{1\,\mathrm{h}}{60\,\mathrm{min}} = 7.5 \times 3.785 = 28.3875 \approx 28.39\,\mathrm{L/min}$.

questions.q: A stock portfolio drops by $20\%$ in Year 1 and drops by another $10\%$ in Year 2. By what percentage must the portfolio grow in Year 3 to return to its exact initial value?
questions.answer: After two years, the value multiplier is $0.80 \times 0.90 = 0.72$. To return to $1.00$, the Year 3 multiplier must be $\dfrac{1}{0.72} = \dfrac{25}{18} \approx 1.3889$, which requires a $38.89\%$ (or $\dfrac{350}{9}\%$) gain.

questions.q: If $a : b = 3 : 4$ and $b : c = 6 : 5$, find the compound ratio $a : b : c$ in lowest integers and evaluate $\dfrac{2a + 3c}{4b}$.

sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: Fresh berries contain $80\%$ water by weight, whereas dried berries contain $20\%$ water by weight. How many kilograms of dried berries are obtained from $50\,\mathrm{kg}$ of fresh berries?
questions.answer: The non-water dry solids remain invariant during drying: $50\,\mathrm{kg}$ of fresh berries contain $(1 - 0.80)(50) = 10\,\mathrm{kg}$ of dry solids. In dried berries, dry solids constitute $1 - 0.20 = 80\%$ of the total mass $M$: $0.80M = 10 \Rightarrow M = 12.5\,\mathrm{kg}$.

questions.q: According to Kepler's Third Law, the square of a planet's orbital period $T$ is directly proportional to the cube of its semi-major axis $a$ ($T^2 = k a^3$). If Planet X has a semi-major axis that is $4$ times that of Earth ($a_E = 1\,\mathrm{AU}, T_E = 1\,\mathrm{yr}$), find Planet X's orbital period and the percentage increase in $T$ when $a$ increases by $21\%$.
questions.answer: For $a = 4$, $T = 4^{3/2} = 8$ Earth years. When $a$ increases by $21\%$, the scale factor for $a$ is $1.21 = (1.1)^2$, so $T$ scales by $(1.21)^{3/2} = (1.1)^3 = 1.331$, which is a $33.1\%$ increase.

questions.q: Two similar right circular cones have surface areas in the ratio $9 : 25$. Find (a) the ratio of their heights, (b) the ratio of their volumes, and (c) the percentage by which the larger cone's volume exceeds the smaller cone's volume.
questions.answer: (a) Linear dimensions scale as the square root of area ratio: $h_1 : h_2 = \sqrt{9} : \sqrt{25} = 3 : 5$. (b) Volumes scale as the cube of linear ratio: $V_1 : V_2 = 3^3 : 5^3 = 27 : 125$. (c) Percentage excess $= \dfrac{125 - 27}{27} \times 100\% = \dfrac{9800}{27}\% \approx 362.96\%$.

questions.q: A medical screening test for a condition present in $2\%$ of a population has a sensitivity (true-positive rate) of $95\%$ and a specificity (true-negative rate) of $90\%$. Out of $10{,}000$ people tested, how many test positive in total, and what percentage of those who test positive actually have the condition (Positive Predictive Value)?
questions.answer: Out of $10{,}000$: $200$ have the condition ($0.95 \times 200 = 190$ true positives) and $9{,}800$ do not ($0.10 \times 9800 = 980$ false positives). Total positive tests $= 190 + 980 = 1{,}170$. Positive Predictive Value $= \dfrac{190}{1170} = \dfrac{19}{117} \approx 16.24\%$.

questions.q: Under continuous-rate radioactive decay, a sample loses $10\%$ of its remaining mass every hour. Write an inequality for the number of hours $t$ until less than $50\%$ of the initial mass remains, and determine the smallest integer hour $t$ that satisfies it.
questions.answer: The remaining fraction after $t$ hours is $(0.90)^t < 0.50$. Testing integer powers: $(0.9)^6 = 0.531441 > 0.50$ and $(0.9)^7 = 0.4782969 < 0.50$. Thus the smallest integer hour is $t = 7$ hours.

questions.target: Quadratic Revenue Elasticity from Percentage Changes
questions.q: An airline increases its ticket price by $p\%$ and observes that ticket sales volume decreases by $\dfrac{p}{2}\%$. Express the percentage change in total revenue as a quadratic function of $p$, and find the non-zero value of $p$ for which total revenue remains unchanged.
questions.answer: Revenue multiplier is $\left(1 + \dfrac{p}{100}\right)\left(1 - \dfrac{p}{200}\right) = 1 + \dfrac{p}{200} - \dfrac{p^2}{20000}$. For revenue to remain unchanged, $\dfrac{p}{200} - \dfrac{p^2}{20000} = 0 \Rightarrow p(100 - p) = 0 \Rightarrow p = 100\%$ (price doubles, volume drops by $50\%$, revenue multiplier $= 2 \times 0.5 = 1$).

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Foundational Concepts (21–28)

questions.q: If $\dfrac{3x}{5y} = \dfrac{9}{10}$, what is the ratio of $x$ to $y$?
questions.answer: Multiply both sides by $\dfrac{5}{3}$: $\dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{9}{10} \cdot \dfrac{5}{3} = \dfrac{3}{2}$, or $3 : 2$.

questions.q: A shirt originally priced at $60$ dollars is on sale for $25\%$ off. If an $8\%$ sales tax is applied to the sale price, what is the final amount paid?
questions.answer: Sale price $= 60(0.75) = 45.00$ dollars. Adding $8\%$ sales tax gives $45.00(1.08) = 48.60$ dollars.

questions.q: A 3D printer produces $18$ identical gears in $45$ minutes. At this constant rate, how many gears can it produce in $2.5$ hours?
questions.answer: Rate $= \dfrac{18\,\mathrm{gears}}{45\,\mathrm{min}} = 0.4\,\mathrm{gears/min}$. In $2.5\,\mathrm{hours} = 150\,\mathrm{minutes}$, output is $0.4 \times 150 = 60$ gears.

questions.q: If $40\%$ of $x$ is equal to $16\%$ of $150$, what is the value of $x$?
A map uses a scale of $1\,\mathrm{inch} = 15\,\mathrm{miles}$. If two cities are $4.6\,\mathrm{inches}$ apart on the map, what is the actual straight-line distance between them?
questions.answer: Multiply $4.6 \times 15 = 69\,\mathrm{miles}$.

questions.q: The price of a commodity increased from $80$ dollars to $100$ dollars. What was the percentage increase?
questions.answer: Percentage increase $= \dfrac{100 - 80}{80} \times 100\% = \dfrac{20}{80} \times 100\% = 25\%$.

questions.q: A fruit punch recipe calls for orange juice and pineapple juice in a ratio of $5 : 3$. How many liters of orange juice are in $24$ liters of punch?
questions.answer: Orange juice makes up $\dfrac{5}{5 + 3} = \dfrac{5}{8}$ of the punch: $\dfrac{5}{8} \times 24 = 15$ liters.

questions.q: If $y$ is directly proportional to $x$, and $y = 18$ when $x = 12$, what is the value of $y$ when $x = 20$?
questions.answer: The constant of proportionality is $k = \dfrac{18}{12} = 1.5$. When $x = 20$, $y = 1.5(20) = 30$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Exam Practice (29–37)

questions.q: The length of a rectangle is increased by $20\%$ and its width is decreased by $15\%$. How does the area of the rectangle change?
questions.answer: Multiply the dimension scale factors: $(1.20)(0.85) = 1.02$, which is a $2\%$ increase in area.

questions.q: Sound intensity $I$ is inversely proportional to the square of distance $r$ from the speaker. If a listener moves from $r = 3\,\mathrm{m}$ to $r = 6\,\mathrm{m}$, the new intensity is what fraction of the original intensity?
questions.answer: Doubling the distance ($r \to 2r$) divides the intensity by $2^2 = 4$, giving $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of the original intensity.

questions.q: How many liters of water must be evaporated from $50\,\mathrm{L}$ of a $12\%$ salt solution to produce a $20\%$ salt solution?
questions.answer: The amount of dissolved salt is constant at $0.12(50) = 6\,\mathrm{L}$. For $6\,\mathrm{L}$ to be $20\%$ of the final volume $V$, $0.20V = 6 \Rightarrow V = 30\,\mathrm{L}$, so $50 - 30 = 20\,\mathrm{L}$ of water must be evaporated.

questions.q: After a $20\%$ discount, the sale price of a coat is $p$ dollars. Which expression represents the original price of the coat before the discount?
questions.answer: Since $0.80 P_0 = p$, we have $P_0 = \dfrac{p}{0.80} = \dfrac{5}{4}p = 1.25p$.

questions.q: An alloy consists of copper and zinc in a $7 : 3$ ratio by mass. If $6\,\mathrm{kg}$ of zinc is added to $40\,\mathrm{kg}$ of this alloy, what is the new ratio of copper to zinc?
questions.answer: Initially, $40\,\mathrm{kg}$ contains $\dfrac{7}{10}(40) = 28\,\mathrm{kg}$ copper and $\dfrac{3}{10}(40) = 12\,\mathrm{kg}$ zinc. Adding $6\,\mathrm{kg}$ zinc gives $18\,\mathrm{kg}$ zinc, so the new ratio is $28 : 18 = 14 : 9$.

questions.q: Titanium has a density of $4.5\,\mathrm{g/cm^3}$. What is the mass, in kilograms, of a solid titanium block with volume $2{,}000\,\mathrm{cm^3}$?
questions.answer: Mass $= 4.5\,\mathrm{g/cm^3} \times 2000\,\mathrm{cm^3} = 9{,}000\,\mathrm{g} = 9.0\,\mathrm{kg}$.

questions.q: Pipe A can fill a tank in $4$ hours, while a drain valve B can empty the full tank in $6$ hours. If both Pipe A and drain valve B are accidentally left open when the tank is empty, how many hours will it take to fill the tank?
questions.answer: Net filling rate $= \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{12} = \dfrac{1}{12}$ tank per hour. Therefore it takes $12$ hours to fill the tank.

questions.q: If $a$ is $25\%$ greater than $b$, and $b$ is $20\%$ less than $c$, then $a$ is what percent of $c$?
questions.answer: Chain the multipliers: $a = 1.25b = 1.25(0.80c) = 1.00c$, so $a$ is $100\%$ of $c$.

questions.target: Harmonic Mean for Equal-Distance Round Trips
questions.q: A cyclist rides uphill at $12\,\mathrm{km/h}$ and immediately rides back down the exact same trail at $36\,\mathrm{km/h}$. What is the cyclist's average speed for the entire round trip?
questions.answer: For equal distances at speeds $v_1$ and $v_2$, the average speed is the harmonic mean: $\dfrac{2 v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2} = \dfrac{2(12)(36)}{12 + 36} = \dfrac{864}{48} = 18\,\mathrm{km/h}$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (38–45)

questions.q: If the radius of a right circular cylinder is increased by $20\%$ and its height is decreased by $25\%$, by what percentage does the volume of the cylinder change?
questions.answer: Since $V = \pi r^2 h$, the volume multiplier is $(1.20)^2(0.75) = 1.44 \times 0.75 = 1.08$, which is an $8\%$ increase.

questions.q: A $10$-liter radiator is filled with a $60\%$ antifreeze solution. How many liters of the solution must be drained and replaced with pure ($100\%$) antifreeze so that the resulting $10$-liter mixture is $75\%$ antifreeze?
questions.answer: If $x$ liters are drained and replaced with pure antifreeze, the antifreeze balance is $0.60(10 - x) + 1.00x = 0.75(10) \Rightarrow 6 + 0.40x = 7.5 \Rightarrow x = 3.75\,\mathrm{L}$.

questions.q: An investment grows at a constant annual compound rate so that its value increases by $44\%$ over $2$ years. What is the percentage increase over $3$ years?
questions.answer: Since $(1 + r)^2 = 1.44$ with $r > 0$, we have $1 + r = 1.20$ ($20\%$ per year). Over $3$ years, $(1.20)^3 = 1.728$, which is a $72.8\%$ increase.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, point $D$ lies on $AB$ such that $AD : DB = 2 : 3$, and point $E$ lies on $AC$ such that $DE \parallel BC$. The area of $\triangle ADE$ is what percent of the area of trapezoid $DBCE$?
questions.answer: Since $AD : AB = 2 : (2 + 3) = 2 : 5$ and $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC$, the area ratio is $[ADE] : [ABC] = 2^2 : 5^2 = 4 : 25$. Thus trapezoid $DBCE$ has relative area $25 - 4 = 21$, and $\dfrac{4}{21} \times 100\% \approx 19.05\%$.

questions.target: Symmetric Percentage Rise & Fall via Quadratics
questions.q: A store raises the price of an item by $x\%$ and later reduces the new price by $x\%$, resulting in a final price that is $9\%$ less than the original price. What is the value of $x$?
questions.answer: The net multiplier is $\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{100}\right)\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{100}\right) = 1 - \dfrac{x^2}{10000} = 1 - 0.09 \Rightarrow \dfrac{x^2}{10000} = 0.09 \Rightarrow x^2 = 900 \Rightarrow x = 30$.

questions.q: In a survey of $500$ voters, the ratio of voters favoring Candidate A to Candidate B is $7 : 3$. How many voters must switch their support from Candidate A to Candidate B so that the new ratio becomes $1 : 1$?
questions.answer: Initially, Candidate A has $\dfrac{7}{10}(500) = 350$ voters and Candidate B has $150$. For a $1 : 1$ split ($250$ each), $350 - 250 = 100$ voters must switch.

questions.target: Gear Ratios & Angular Velocity in Radians
questions.q: Two gears are meshed together. Gear A has $36$ teeth and rotates at $150\,\mathrm{rpm}$. If Gear B has $24$ teeth, through how many radians does Gear B rotate in $2$ seconds?
questions.answer: By inverse tooth ratio, Gear B rotates at $150 \times \dfrac{36}{24} = 225\,\mathrm{rpm} = \dfrac{225}{60} = 3.75\,\mathrm{rev/s}$. In $2$ seconds, Gear B completes $7.5$ revolutions, which is $7.5 \times 2\pi = 15\pi$ radians.

questions.q: If $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d} = \dfrac{3}{4}$ with $b + 2d \neq 0$, what is the value of $\dfrac{a + 2c}{b + 2d}$?
questions.answer: Since $a = \dfrac{3}{4}b$ and $c = \dfrac{3}{4}d$, we have $\dfrac{a + 2c}{b + 2d} = \dfrac{\frac{3}{4}(b + 2d)}{b + 2d} = \dfrac{3}{4}$ by the mediant property of equal ratios.
